requirements.text: Transferring assets within the same department does not require a request.
Inter-departmental asset transfers must be approved by a DA group member and a faculty group member unless initiated by a higher level group.
Inter-faculty asset transfers must be approved by a faculty group or higher level.
Asset transfers outside the university must be approved by the university group.
Authorized administrative or inventory users can edit assets belonging to their department, faculty, or university.
All fields of an edited asset can be modified except for IDs.
A bulk entry file can be used for modifying assets.
A bulk entry can be used to add many assets.
Requests can be made by any authorized user.
An inventory user must check returned assets and update the inventory.
IT group members can create a new space and modify floor structure upon receiving an exception request from an administrative level.
Any administration level or authorized inventory group member can display and approve pending requests within their authority.
Users are notified by email when a request is treated.
Authentication is performed using a username and password for all users.
Administrative level users can delegate another user to execute some or all of their authorized actions.
All user passwords must meet a minimum complexity standard (e.g., 12 characters, mixed case, numbers, and symbols) and sessions must automatically terminate after 15 minutes of inactivity.
The system must maintain an immutable audit log of all asset modifications, permission changes, and approval actions, including the timestamp, user ID, and action taken.
All database backups must be encrypted at rest and access to backup files must be restricted to authorized IT personnel only.
The system shall maintain 99.9% availability during university working hours, with a maximum recovery time of 4 hours for critical failures.
The system shall terminate any database query that exceeds 60 seconds of execution time under a peak load of 500 concurrent users.
The system shall be designed using a modular architecture with a maximum cyclomatic complexity of 15 per method to facilitate future evolution.
Define maximum latency for common operations: 'The system shall return search results within 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.'
Define constraints for bulk operations: 'The system shall process bulk asset imports of up to 1,000 records within 30 seconds.'

OPEN: The PRD mentions 'email' notification for request status but does not specify if sensitive data will be included in these emails. - System-generated email notifications must not include sensitive asset details or PII; they should only contain a link to the secure portal to view the status.

OPEN: The backup requirement lacks frequency, retention policy, and recovery point objective (RPO). - The system shall perform automated daily incremental backups and weekly full backups, with a retention period of 30 days and an RPO of 24 hours.

OPEN: The PRD lacks information regarding the expected number of concurrent users, total asset count, or transaction volume. - Specify the expected load: 'The system shall support at least 50 concurrent users and a database of 100,000 assets without performance degradation.'
